The studio was called "Eternal Stillness," a name that felt increasingly ironic as the clock ticked toward 7:00 PM. Jim stood near the back, clutching his mat like a shield. He had intended to join the "Intro to Mindfulness" class, but a misread flyer and a case of mistaken identity had landed him in "Advanced Vinyasa Flow: The Ascension."

The instructor, a woman named Seraphina who looked like she hadn’t touched the ground since 1998, glided to the front. "Today," she whispered, her voice echoing in the silent room, "we seek the balance of the crane. We extend our necks to touch the heavens, releasing all tension."

Jim looked around. Everyone else was already in a graceful, elongated pose, their chins tilted up, eyes closed in serene concentration. Jim, a man whose idea of stretching was reaching for the remote without standing up, panicked. He didn't know what a crane pose was, but he knew he needed to look like he belonged. He remembered seeing something on TV where people stretched their necks. He decided to mimic the person next to him, who was currently doing a handstand.

Jim attempted to lift his chest and stretch his neck upward. However, lacking the core strength of a yogi and the flexibility of a gymnast, his body interpreted the command differently. As he arched his back to simulate the "long neck" of a crane, he inadvertently compressed his diaphragm.

The first sound was a low, guttural grunt, like a bear waking up from hibernation. It wasn't a meditative hum; it was the sound of a man realizing he had made a terrible mistake.

Seraphina opened one eye. "Breathe, Jim. Let the energy flow."

Jim tried to breathe. He inhaled deeply, trying to relax his abdominal muscles. This was a critical error. The combination of the awkward arch, the tight yoga pants, and the sheer panic in his system created a perfect storm. As he exhaled, attempting to find his zen, his body released a sound that was less "spiritual awakening" and more "deflating tire."

It was a long, resonant toot that seemed to vibrate through the floorboards.

The class froze. The woman doing the handstand wobbled. The man in the lotus position cracked an eye open.
